svg.title: Fetal heart rate decelerations
svg.desc: Four fetal monitoring strips drawn out - early, late, variable decelerations and an acceleration - each with the contraction traced underneath it and a dashed line through the peak of the contraction, so the timing that tells them apart is visible. Below them, the intervention order for a late deceleration.
svg.text: READING THE STRIP — VEAL CHOP, DRAWN OUT
The shape of the dip and where it sits against the contraction is the entire question.
Nadir sits directly under the peak. It mirrors it.
Starts after the peak. Still recovering when it is over.
Left side · stop oxytocin · O₂ · fluids · call
Abrupt V or W. It ignores the contraction entirely.
The rate rises. This is the reassuring one.
Nothing. This is a healthy foetus.
⚠ LATE DECELERATION — THE ORDER, EVERY TIME
Why the left side: supine, the uterus presses on the inferior vena cava → venous return falls
→ cardiac output falls → placental flow falls. Turning her left lifts the uterus off the vessel.
